verdict.rationale: kitty's first-party ssh kitten logs into remote hosts and automatically sets up the remote environment. It documents automatic shell integration, file transfer, connection reuse and remote-control socket forwarding. Community complaints about xterm-kitty terminfo breaking on remote servers describe plain ssh use, not a failure of the kitten, so they don't create a dispute. missing for 10: explicit documentation that the kitten copies terminfo to the remote host, explicit documentation of carrying local config/dotfiles along, hands-on or independent corroboration of the kitten working.

support.subject: As a developer, I can SSH to remote hosts with the terminal's own integration carrying my terminfo, shell integration, and config along

citations.quote: The ssh kitten allows you to login easily to remote hosts, and automatically setup the environment there to be as comfortable as your local shell; automatic shell integration, file transfer and reuse of connections, plus automatic forwarding of remote control sockets.
